title: NumPy Copying Arrays and Understanding Views
learningObjectives: Explain numpy copying arrays and understanding views and its role in numerical Python.
Choose the appropriate NumPy operation for a given data task.
Predict array shapes, values and memory behavior before execution.
Write clear NumPy code and interpret its output.
Recognize common edge cases and validate assumptions.

understand.concept: NumPy distinguishes independent copies from views that share the same underlying data. A view can reflect changes made through either reference, while a copy owns independent data. Use np.shares_memory when you need to verify whether two arrays overlap in memory; do not infer sharing only from object identity.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding memory sharing prevents accidental mutation of source data and helps avoid unnecessary allocations when working with large numerical datasets.
understand.analogy: Think of an array as a structured tray of values: its dimensions describe the compartments, and each operation determines whether values are shared, rearranged or selected.

explain.narrative: Read the explanation, trace the dimensions and values, and run each example. The examples use deterministic inputs so their output can be checked exactly. examples.title: Create an independent copy
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
b = a.copy()
b[0] = 99
print(a.tolist(), b.tolist())
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create an independent copy using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Create a view
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
v = a.view()
v[1] = 8
print(a.tolist())
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create a view using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Check shared memory
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.arange(4)
v = a[1:]
c = a.copy()
print(np.shares_memory(a, v), np.shares_memory(a, c))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates check shared memory using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Change the source through a view
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([4, 5, 6])
v = a.view()
a[2] = 10
print(v.tolist())
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates change the source through a view using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Copy a slice before editing
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([2, 4, 6, 8])
part = a[1:3].copy()
part[:] = 0
print(a.tolist(), part.tolist())
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates copy a slice before editing using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.
